questions.prompt: In the indiscrete topology on a set X, the only open sets are ∅ and X.
questions.explanation: That is the definition of the indiscrete topology.

questions.prompt: How many open sets are there in the discrete topology on a 3-point set?
questions.explanation: Every subset is open, and a 3-element set has 2³ = 8 subsets.

questions.prompt: Which collections are topologies on X = {a, b, c}?
questions.explanation: The second lacks {a, b} = {a} ∪ {b}; the fourth lacks X.

questions.prompt: A function f: X → Y is continuous exactly when:
choices: The preimage of every open set is open
The image of every open set is open
The preimage of every point is open
questions.answer: The preimage of every open set is open
questions.explanation: This is the topological definition of continuity.

questions.prompt: A continuous bijection whose inverse is also continuous is called a ___.
questions.explanation: Homeomorphisms are the isomorphisms of topology.

questions.prompt: [0, 1) is open in the subspace topology on [0, 1] inherited from ℝ.
questions.explanation: [0, 1) = (−1, 1) ∩ [0, 1], an open set of ℝ intersected with the subspace.

questions.prompt: Which of these subsets of ℝ is connected?
questions.explanation: Intervals are the connected subsets of ℝ; the others can be split by open sets.

questions.prompt: Every path-connected space is connected.
questions.explanation: A separation would force a path to jump between two disjoint open sets, contradicting continuity.

questions.prompt: Which of these subspaces are path-connected?
questions.explanation: The other two are disconnected, so no path joins their pieces.

questions.prompt: Which subset of ℝ is compact?
questions.explanation: Heine-Borel: compact in ℝⁿ means closed and bounded.

questions.prompt: Every closed subset of ℝ is compact.
questions.explanation: [0, ∞) is closed but unbounded, and the open cover {(−1, n)} has no finite subcover.

questions.prompt: Prove that the continuous image of a compact space is compact.
rubric: Starts with an open cover of f(K)
Takes preimages, which are open by continuity and cover K
Extracts a finite subcover of K
Maps the finite subcover back to cover f(K)
questions.model: Let f: K → Y be continuous with K compact, and let {Uᵢ} cover f(K) by open sets. The preimages f⁻¹(Uᵢ) are open and cover K, so finitely many cover K. The corresponding Uᵢ then cover f(K).
questions.explanation: Continuity pulls open covers back, compactness extracts a finite piece, and the images give a finite subcover.

questions.prompt: Match each space to its construction.
pairs: Square with opposite edges identified (S¹ × S¹)
Rectangle with one pair of edges glued with a twist
questions.explanation: Each space is a product or quotient of simpler ones.

questions.prompt: The sets U × V with U open in X and V open in Y form a basis for the product topology on X × Y.
questions.explanation: That is the definition of the product topology.

questions.prompt: In the quotient topology induced by q: X → X/∼, a set U ⊆ X/∼ is open exactly when:
questions.explanation: The quotient topology is the finest topology making q continuous.

questions.prompt: Every metric space is Hausdorff.
questions.explanation: For x ≠ y, the open balls of radius d(x, y)/2 are disjoint.

questions.prompt: What name is given to a space where any two distinct points have disjoint open neighborhoods?
questions.explanation: This is the Hausdorff (T₂) condition.

questions.prompt: Which spaces are Hausdorff?
choices: An indiscrete space with at least 2 points
An infinite set with the finite-complement topology
questions.explanation: The indiscrete and cofinite topologies have no disjoint neighborhoods of distinct points.

questions.prompt: The fundamental group of the circle S¹ is isomorphic to:
questions.explanation: Loops are classified by their winding number.

questions.prompt: A contractible space has trivial fundamental group.
questions.explanation: Every loop can be continuously shrunk to the basepoint.

questions.prompt: Explain why [0, 1] and (0, 1) are not homeomorphic.
rubric: Uses that compactness is preserved by homeomorphism
questions.model: [0, 1] is compact by Heine-Borel while (0, 1) is not, since the cover by intervals (1/n, 1) has no finite subcover. Compactness is a topological property preserved by homeomorphisms, so the two spaces cannot be homeomorphic.
questions.explanation: A topological invariant (compactness) distinguishes them.
